primary_competency: Patient Care: Diagnosis, including history and physical examination
mechanism: Autoantibodies against phospholipid-binding proteins promote arterial and venous thrombosis and recurrent pregnancy morbidity despite possible prolongation of phospholipid-dependent clotting assays in vitro.
vignette: A 31-year-old woman has two prior deep venous thromboses and three unexplained pregnancy losses. PTT is prolonged, but she has no bleeding history.
distractor_notes: Hemophilia causes bleeding and is X-linked, not thrombosis and recurrent pregnancy loss.
Von Willebrand disease causes mucocutaneous bleeding.
Protein C deficiency causes venous thrombosis but does not characteristically cause prolonged PTT or recurrent pregnancy loss from antiphospholipid antibodies.
ITP causes thrombocytopenic bleeding rather than recurrent thrombosis.
key_expl: Recurrent thrombosis and pregnancy loss with a paradoxically prolonged phospholipid-dependent PTT is classic antiphospholipid syndrome.
objective: Recognize antiphospholipid syndrome from thrombosis, pregnancy morbidity, and lupus anticoagulant physiology.
clues: recurrent pregnancy loss with prolonged PTT

primary_competency: Medical Knowledge: Applying Foundational Science Concepts
mechanism: Porphobilinogen deaminase deficiency causes accumulation of porphyrin precursors, producing episodic neurovisceral symptoms without photosensitivity.
vignette: A 24-year-old woman has recurrent severe abdominal pain, anxiety, peripheral neuropathy, and darkening urine after starting a CYP-inducing medication. There is no photosensitive rash.
lead: Which enzyme is most likely deficient?
distractor_notes: Uroporphyrinogen decarboxylase deficiency causes porphyria cutanea tarda with photosensitivity.
Ferrochelatase deficiency causes erythropoietic protoporphyria.
ALA dehydratase deficiency is a rare porphyria and also inhibited by lead, but is not classic AIP.
Heme oxygenase degrades heme rather than synthesizing it.
key_expl: AIP is caused by porphobilinogen deaminase deficiency and causes acute neurovisceral attacks without cutaneous photosensitivity.
objective: Differentiate acute intermittent porphyria from cutaneous porphyrias.
clues: triggered by CYP-inducing drug without photosensitivity

primary_competency: Medical Knowledge: Applying Foundational Science Concepts
mechanism: Uroporphyrinogen decarboxylase deficiency causes porphyrin accumulation and blistering photosensitivity on sun-exposed skin, often with hepatic risk factors.
vignette: A 48-year-old man has fragile blistering skin on the backs of his hands after sun exposure and hyperpigmentation. He has no recurrent neurovisceral attacks.
distractor_notes: Porphobilinogen deaminase deficiency causes AIP without the classic photosensitive blistering skin disease.
Glucose-6-phosphatase deficiency causes GSD I.
Phenylalanine hydroxylase deficiency causes PKU.
CBS deficiency causes homocystinuria.
key_expl: Porphyria cutanea tarda results from deficient uroporphyrinogen decarboxylase and presents with photosensitive blistering.
objective: Identify the enzyme defect in porphyria cutanea tarda.

primary_competency: Medical Knowledge: Applying Foundational Science Concepts
mechanism: Deficiency of methylmalonyl-CoA mutase or its cobalamin cofactor pathway prevents conversion of methylmalonyl-CoA to succinyl-CoA, causing metabolic acidosis and neurologic toxicity.
vignette: A newborn develops poor feeding, vomiting, lethargy, and high-anion-gap metabolic acidosis. Methylmalonic acid is markedly elevated.
distractor_notes: Propionyl-CoA carboxylase catalyzes the preceding step and is deficient in propionic acidemia.
Phenylalanine hydroxylase deficiency causes PKU.
CBS deficiency causes homocystinuria.
Glucose-6-phosphatase deficiency causes GSD I.
key_expl: Methylmalonyl-CoA mutase converts methylmalonyl-CoA to succinyl-CoA and requires vitamin B12-derived adenosylcobalamin.
objective: Identify the blocked metabolic reaction in methylmalonic acidemia.

primary_competency: Medical Knowledge: Applying Foundational Science Concepts
mechanism: Propionyl-CoA carboxylase deficiency blocks conversion of propionyl-CoA to methylmalonyl-CoA, causing toxic organic acid accumulation, metabolic acidosis, hyperammonemia, and neonatal illness.
vignette: A neonate develops vomiting, lethargy, metabolic acidosis, and hyperammonemia. Genetic testing shows biallelic PCCA variants.
distractor_notes: Propionyl-CoA carboxylase uses biotin, not PLP.
It is not an FAD dehydrogenase.
It does not use heme as its defining cofactor.
It is not a zinc protease.
key_expl: Propionyl-CoA carboxylase is a biotin-dependent enzyme.
objective: Connect propionic acidemia with a biotin-dependent carboxylase defect.

primary_competency: Medical Knowledge: Applying Foundational Science Concepts
mechanism: Fumarylacetoacetate hydrolase deficiency causes accumulation of toxic tyrosine metabolites including succinylacetone, leading to liver failure and renal tubular dysfunction.
vignette: An infant has liver failure, renal tubular dysfunction, and a cabbage-like odor. Succinylacetone is elevated.
lead: Which enzyme is most likely deficient?
distractor_notes: Tyrosine hydroxylase participates in catecholamine synthesis.
Homogentisate dioxygenase deficiency causes alkaptonuria.
Phenylalanine hydroxylase deficiency causes PKU.
BCKD deficiency causes MSUD.
key_expl: Tyrosinemia type I is caused by FAH deficiency and is marked by succinylacetone accumulation.
objective: Identify the enzyme defect in tyrosinemia type I.

primary_competency: Medical Knowledge: Applying Foundational Science Concepts
mechanism: Argininosuccinate lyase deficiency blocks cleavage of argininosuccinate to arginine and fumarate, causing hyperammonemia and argininosuccinate accumulation.
vignette: A child has episodic hyperammonemia and elevated argininosuccinic acid.
distractors: Carbamoyl phosphate plus ornithine to citrulline
Ammonia plus bicarbonate to carbamoyl phosphate
distractor_notes: Argininosuccinate synthetase performs this preceding step.
OTC converts carbamoyl phosphate and ornithine to citrulline.
Arginase cleaves arginine to ornithine and urea.
CPS1 forms carbamoyl phosphate.
key_expl: Argininosuccinate lyase produces arginine and fumarate from argininosuccinate.
objective: Localize a urea-cycle block from the accumulating intermediate.

primary_competency: Medical Knowledge: Applying Foundational Science Concepts
mechanism: Argininosuccinate synthetase deficiency blocks condensation of citrulline with aspartate, causing citrulline accumulation and hyperammonemia.
vignette: A neonate develops severe hyperammonemia with markedly elevated plasma citrulline.
lead: Which enzyme is most likely deficient?
distractor_notes: OTC deficiency often has low citrulline and elevated orotic acid.
Arginase deficiency raises arginine.
CPS1 deficiency causes low citrulline without orotic acid elevation.
ASL deficiency causes argininosuccinate accumulation.
key_expl: Citrullinemia type I is caused by ASS1 deficiency and elevated citrulline.
objective: Identify argininosuccinate synthetase deficiency from hypercitrullinemia.

primary_competency: Medical Knowledge: Applying Foundational Science Concepts
mechanism: ATP7A deficiency impairs intestinal copper export and delivery to copper-dependent enzymes, causing neurodegeneration, connective-tissue abnormalities, and kinky sparse hair.
vignette: A 4-month-old boy has seizures, developmental regression, failure to thrive, and sparse brittle kinky hair. Serum copper is low.
lead: Which transport protein is most likely defective?
distractor_notes: ATP7B deficiency causes Wilson disease with copper accumulation.
CFTR causes cystic fibrosis.
LDLR defects cause familial hypercholesterolemia.
ABCD1 defects cause X-linked adrenoleukodystrophy.
key_expl: Menkes disease results from ATP7A dysfunction and impaired systemic copper distribution.
objective: Differentiate Menkes from Wilson disease by copper transport protein and phenotype.
clues: kinky hair and neurodegeneration in infancy

primary_competency: Medical Knowledge: Applying Foundational Science Concepts
mechanism: C1 esterase inhibitor deficiency permits excess kallikrein activity and bradykinin generation, causing recurrent nonpruritic edema without urticaria.
vignette: A 20-year-old woman has recurrent episodes of painless swelling of the lips and hands and occasional severe abdominal pain. There is no urticaria. Her father has similar episodes.
distractor_notes: Histamine-mediated angioedema usually accompanies urticaria and allergic symptoms.
Serotonin is not the primary mediator of hereditary angioedema.
Thromboxane A2 mediates platelet activation and vasoconstriction.
IL-5 promotes eosinophil growth and activation.
key_expl: Hereditary C1 inhibitor deficiency causes bradykinin-mediated angioedema without urticaria.
objective: Differentiate bradykinin-mediated hereditary angioedema from allergic histamine-mediated edema.
